groups.statement: The X-Ray Telescope flight software shall keep the telescope operating reliably.
The X-Ray Telescope flight software shall collect high-quality data on gamma-ray bursts and their afterglows.
The X-Ray Telescope flight software shall downlink science data to the ground.
In normal operations, the software shall accept commands.
In normal operations, the software shall maintain the instrument’s operating state.
In normal operations, the software shall acquire detector data.
In normal operations, the software shall process detector data into useful scientific products.
In normal operations, the software shall package scientific products for transmission.
The software shall continuously monitor its own health.
The software shall support safe recovery actions when something goes wrong in the space environment.
The software shall handle routine, well-understood faults onboard.
The software shall handle transient command errors onboard.
The software shall handle minor communication glitches onboard.
The software shall handle brief detector anomalies onboard.
The software shall handle recoverable processing faults onboard.
The software shall be allowed to retry operations.
The software shall be allowed to reset affected software tasks or interfaces.
The software shall be allowed to reinitialize the instrument state.
The software shall be allowed to take the telescope to a predefined safe configuration if needed.
The software shall escalate to safe mode if a fault is persistent.
The software shall escalate to safe mode if it cannot confirm recovery after a limited number of attempts.
The software shall report the condition so ground operators can decide the next step.
Detector data and any partially built science products shall be treated as protected mission data.
The software shall provide a durable queue or storage area that survives resets and short interruptions.
If processing is interrupted, the system shall be able to resume from the last consistent point or reconstruct the product from saved raw and intermediate data.
The system shall avoid restarting processing if doing so would risk data loss.
If storage starts to fill or a fault persists, the system shall preserve the highest-priority data first.
The system shall clearly mark incomplete products.
The system shall keep incomplete products available for later downlink once the telescope is stable again.
The X-Ray Telescope software shall support the normal mission startup state.
The X-Ray Telescope software shall support the standby or idle state.
The X-Ray Telescope software shall support the science acquisition state.
The X-Ray Telescope software shall support the safe mode state.
The X-Ray Telescope software shall support the recovery or reconfiguration states.
The software shall allow state changes only when the command source is authorized.
The software shall allow state changes only when safety checks show the instrument is in a condition where the transition will not damage hardware or corrupt data.
If the authorization, validity, or safety checks fail, the software shall reject the command.
If the authorization, validity, or safety checks fail, the software shall leave the current state unchanged.
At startup, the software shall first bring up the basic processor and communication interfaces.
The software shall verify that essential subsystems are responding and that no critical faults are latched.
The software shall initialize the instrument hardware after bringing up the basic processor and communication interfaces and verifying subsystem health.
The software shall load or restore the last known safe state if appropriate.
The software shall run any required self-checks or calibrations needed to confirm that the detector and control paths are usable.

Startup shall be considered complete only once the required checks pass, the operating state is validated, and the telescope is confirmed safe to transition into standby or science acquisition if commanded and allowed.
A command shall be accepted only if it is authorized.
A command shall be accepted only if it is permitted in the current operating state.
Science commands shall be blocked in safe mode.
Risky reconfiguration or calibration commands shall be allowed only in the appropriate maintenance or transition states.
Routine monitoring or housekeeping commands shall generally remain available.
The software shall check parameter ranges.
The software shall check sequencing dependencies.
The software shall check timing.
A command shall be invalid if it arrives before a required prerequisite.
A command shall be invalid if it conflicts with an active operation.
A command shall be invalid if it would move the instrument into an unsafe or inconsistent state.
The flight software shall interact with onboard control logic and autonomous fault-management functions.
Onboard control logic and autonomous fault-management functions shall have authority to manage routine operations and take immediate protective actions when needed.
The flight software shall interact with ground operators and mission planning systems that provide commanded activities, configuration updates, and recovery decisions.
Ground operators and mission planning systems shall have indirect authority that is filtered through command validation and state checks.
The flight software shall interface with telemetry and downlink systems to package housekeeping and science products for transmission.
Telemetry and downlink system interfaces shall not be able to override safety logic.
The flight software shall monitor its own execution health.
The flight software shall monitor detector and control hardware status.
The flight software shall monitor power and thermal conditions.
The flight software shall monitor communication link health.
The flight software shall monitor active fault and recovery actions.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include the current operating mode.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include the last command received and whether it was accepted.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include fault flags.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include reset or retry counts.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include data backlog or buffer usage.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include key subsystem temperatures and voltages.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include a clear indication of whether the instrument is in normal operation.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include a clear indication of whether the instrument is in degraded operation.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include a clear indication of whether the instrument is in safe mode.
Housekeeping telemetry shall include timestamps and sequence markers.
Housekeeping telemetry shall indicate whether telemetry or science products are missing.
Housekeeping telemetry shall indicate whether telemetry or science products are delayed.
Housekeeping telemetry shall indicate whether telemetry or science products are being recovered.
The software shall always prioritize safety and status telemetry first.
The software shall prioritize critical fault and recovery information after safety and status telemetry.
The software shall transmit science products and lower-priority housekeeping only after safety and status telemetry and critical fault and recovery information.
If bandwidth is tight, the software shall throttle nonessential streams.
If bandwidth is tight, the software shall bundle or compress products where possible.
If bandwidth is tight, the software shall queue any remaining data for the next downlink opportunity without discarding anything important.
When storage pressure becomes severe, the software may delay the oldest or lowest-priority noncritical data.
The software shall protect fault context, incomplete products, and any data needed to reconstruct recent observations, and send them ahead of routine data.

groups.statement: The flight software shall support command handling for the X-Ray Telescope control processor.
The flight software shall support data acquisition and processing for the X-Ray Telescope control processor.
The flight software shall support fault monitoring and recovery for the X-Ray Telescope control processor.
The control processor flight software shall support operations in orbit.
The instrument shall reliably collect science data.
The system shall receive commands from the ground and execute them through the control processor.
The system shall collect detector data during observations.
The system shall use onboard monitoring for fault handling.
The flight software shall be more reliable.
The flight software shall provide smoother command execution.
The system shall provide good health and status reporting so the ground team can understand what the telescope is doing without digging through raw telemetry.
The system shall provide more robust logging or diagnostic information for anomalies if it is in scope for the release.
The depth of anomaly logging may depend on storage and downlink constraints.
The anomaly logging depth shall undergo engineering review.
The system shall prioritize command handling and state management first.
The system shall protect the instrument while the rest of the functionality comes online.
The software shall check whether the incoming command is allowed in the current operating state.
If the command is valid, the software shall hand it to the appropriate internal handler.
After executing a valid command, the software shall update the state model to reflect any result.
If the command is not valid or execution fails, the software shall reject the command or flag the error.
The telescope system shall support a safe or standby condition.
The telescope system shall support an initialization or boot-up state.
The telescope system shall support a normal science-operating state.
The telescope system shall support a fault or recovery state.
The telescope shall remain in a low-risk configuration in safe or standby state.
In safe or standby state, the telescope shall report health.
Initialization or boot-up shall bring the control processor and X-Ray Telescope software into a known-good starting condition after power-up or reset.
In normal science-operating state, the telescope shall actively collect detector data.
In fault or recovery state, the system shall stop or limit activities that might worsen the problem.
The software shall reject the command cleanly and not execute any part of it.
The software shall report the current operating state.
The software shall package the information so ground operators can receive it during downlink.
The system shall accept raw detector telemetry.
The system shall validate raw detector telemetry.
The system shall transform raw detector telemetry into science and housekeeping outputs used for operations and downlink.
The system shall perform basic formatting on the data.
The system shall time-tag the data.
The system shall apply any required filtering or buffering so the data can be stored and transmitted reliably.
The flight software shall prepare science data records for ground analysis and operations.
The flight software shall prepare supporting housekeeping and status products for ground analysis and operations.
The flight software shall package processed detector events or summaries in the format expected by the downlink path.
The flight software shall include metadata needed to interpret the downlinked products later.
The exact product definitions and formats shall come from the science and ground system teams.
Detector and instrument engineers shall be considered because they understand the hardware capabilities and the failure modes that need protection.
The flight operations team and ground system personnel shall be considered because they know how commands, telemetry, and recovery are handled in practice.
The science team shall be involved so that onboard processing and downlink products support the actual mission data needs rather than only the software’s technical needs.
The flight software shall boot reliably on the control processor.
The flight software shall downlink expected detector data without losing important information.
The flight software shall support stable autonomous operation with no surprises.
The system shall ensure that detector data and command responses are synchronized with spacecraft time very accurately.
The software shall be cautious about resource limits, including memory and buffer handling.
The software shall account for the fact that it operates in a constrained flight environment and cannot assume it can recover from overload as it would on the ground.
The interviewee will review the summary carefully when it is sent over.
The interviewee will flag any corrections or clarifications needed in the summary.
